description: `cli-health generate-manifest <scenario>` bootstraps a valid `cli/manifest.json` for any scenario that currently lacks one, lowering the barrier to adoption.

requirements.description: The `cli-health generate-manifest <scenario>` command must generate a valid `cli/manifest.json` file for any scenario that does not already have one, by introspecting that scenario's existing compiled proto descriptor set. The generated manifest must: list all discovered RPC methods as command bindings with auto-inferred names, pass schema validation (`cli-health validate`) with zero error findings immediately after generation, and not overwrite an existing `cli/manifest.json` without an explicit `--force` flag.
requirements.title: Manifest Scaffolding from Existing Proto Descriptors

validation.notes: Given a descriptor set with 3 RPC methods and no existing manifest, generate-manifest produces a manifest with 3 binding entries
Given an existing cli/manifest.json without --force, generate-manifest exits nonzero and does not overwrite
Given --force flag with an existing manifest, generate-manifest overwrites the file
Given an auto-generated manifest, immediately running cli-health validate returns zero error-level findings
Run generate-manifest against a test scenario that has a descriptor set but no manifest; assert the generated file passes `cli-health validate` with exit code 0
Run generate-manifest against one of the 6 adopting scenarios without --force; assert no file modification occurs
New scenarios can adopt cli-health in a single command rather than hand-authoring manifest JSON, accelerating onboarding

title: Manifest scaffolding command
